assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a coherent arc from peptide biology to transformative treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large, durable clinical and physiological impact and clear relevance to the Nobel criterion of benefit to humankind.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 secretion and actions in humans) and Drucker (GLP-1 biology, proglucagon processing, translation to therapy) are the strongest physiological anchors; Mojsov is credited for identifying the active GLP-1(7-36) form. Knudsen (drug development) is a strong industrial contributor but a three-person limit forces a choice, and credit among early peptide-identification contributors is contested.
assessment.maturity: Therapies are widely confirmed in large independent trials and approved for several indications; recognition is timely and arguably overdue given the field's scale.
uncertainties: Allocation between basic discoverers (Holst, Drucker, Mojsov) and drug developers (Knudsen) is unresolved.
I rely on recalled knowledge of the priority dispute over GLP-1 identification and have not verified it.
Long-term safety and outcome data are still accruing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors created a new class of living therapy, producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas; the concept is original and the clinical impact large.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June drove the design and clinical translation of CAR-T constructs (including costimulation), while Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. Eshhar's foundational contribution is not among the credited names, which complicates fairness.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation in hematologic cancers; durability data now exist, though solid-tumor extension and toxicity management remain evolving.
uncertainties: Missing foundational credit (e.g., original chimeric receptor concept) is not available among supplied names.
Limited efficacy in solid tumors and long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity with millisecond precision and transformed circuit analysis, including studies of motor and behavioral circuits. Originality and breadth of impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterized channelrhodopsins as light-gated channels; Deisseroth and Boyden established neuronal use in mammalian systems; Miesenböck made earlier genetically targeted light-control demonstrations. Six credited names exceed three slots and a fair split is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature tool with thousands of independent applications; clinical translation (retinal optogenetic therapy) is early, but the basic discovery is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely contested among at least six scientists and I cannot resolve it.
The discovery is partly a tool, so the committee may weigh methods versus a discovery about nature or disease.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signaling pathway from the ER to the nucleus, with deep conceptual originality and implications for secretory physiology, metabolic disease, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Mori and Walter independently elucidated the IRE1-HAC1/XBP1 pathway and its signaling logic, a clean two-person configuration; other contributors (e.g., Ron, Harding) are not in the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is thoroughly confirmed over three decades and textbook-level; recognition is timely, with therapeutic modulation still developing.
uncertainties: Whether other UPR branch discoverers (PERK/ATF6) would be seen as necessary for fair credit is unclear.
Medical impact is mostly indirect compared with therapeutic candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway revealed how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, connecting infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunotherapy; a clear mechanistic discovery with growing translational relevance.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger, and Barber discovered STING; Ishikawa co-discovered STING, and Sun and Wu contributed to the cGAS work in Chen's laboratory. Chen and Barber are the most defensible pair, though other contributors have claims.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism well replicated; therapeutic agents are still in clinical development, so impact on patients is not yet proven.
uncertainties: Credit for STING discovery is shared with Ishikawa and others.
Clinical benefit of pathway-targeting drugs is unproven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCR-ABL inhibition with imatinib turned CML from a fatal into a chronic disease and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy; very high clinical significance.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (compound development at Ciba-Geigy) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a plausible trio; the underlying BCR-ABL and kinase discoveries by others (e.g., Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of clinical follow-up and independent confirmation make this fully mature, though one might argue the fundamental discoveries were already recognized.
uncertainties: Industrial and clinical development credit is more diffuse than a three-name list suggests.
The Committee has historically preferred conceptual discoveries over drug development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is the leading cellular model of synaptic plasticity, learning and memory, with foundational importance across neuroscience.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo made the original 1973 discovery; Collingridge identified NMDA receptor dependence; Morris linked LTP to spatial memory behaviorally. Credit across four names is plausible but allocation requires choice.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed for decades; the link between LTP and memory is supported but the full causal relationship remains debated, and the discovery is very old.
uncertainties: The causal role of LTP in memory is still debated.
Choice between Collingridge and Morris for the third place is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identified a neuropeptide system essential for wakefulness and the cause of narcolepsy type 1, a clear discovery of a specific neural mechanism with therapeutic follow-up (orexin receptor antagonists and agonists).
assessment.attribution: Sakurai and Yanagisawa discovered orexins and their receptors; de Lecea and Kilduff independently identified hypocretin; Mignot's canine narcolepsy gene work linked the receptor to disease. Priority is shared and the sensible three-person split is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed with approved drugs for insomnia; narcolepsy agonists are in late-stage development, so the translational story is still maturing.
uncertainties: Parallel independent discovery by the Scripps group complicates attribution.
Agonist therapy for narcolepsy is not yet established.
